headline: Trump and Zelensky will meet in New York this week
summary: Zelensky said Sunday that he and President Trump will meet this week in New York, during the UN General Assembly, after a phone call he said “could change a lot.” Ukraine's negotiator told Axios the sticking points are down from dozens to one or two. A source said Trump kept asking Zelensky to stop hitting Russian oil refineries.
cover_answer: They did call Sunday. Now they'll sit down together.
table_question: If a friend helps you, do they get a say in how you use it?

5-7.script: Ukraine is a country that has been fighting a war for years. On Sunday its leader called President Trump, and they agreed to meet in New York this week to talk about how to stop it. It's like two people who keep texting about a problem and finally decide to sit at the same table. Nobody has fixed it yet, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: One phone call, one table. A five-year-old has watched grown-ups do exactly this.
5-7.why_long: A five-year-old reasons from what is in front of them and reads your face before your words, so the script keeps the war offstage and puts two people at a table, which they have seen. The refineries and the diesel stay out. Expect “will they stop the war?” Say the truth: they are trying, and nobody knows yet.

8-12.script: Ukraine hits Russia's oil refineries to drain the money that pays for the war. That raises diesel prices everywhere, so Trump keeps asking them to stop. On Sunday the two agreed to meet Tuesday. A checklist with dozens of boxes: Ukraine's negotiator says one or two are left.
8-12.why: A chain: strikes, diesel, a call, a meeting. Then a checklist they can count.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect, and this story is a clean chain: refinery strikes raise diesel prices, so Trump asks for them to stop, so the two meet. The checklist is the mechanism, dozens of items down to one or two. Expect “so is the war ending?” Not yet. One or two items can still be the hard ones.

13-17.script: If an ally sends you weapons and sanctions your enemy, does he get to pick your targets? Trump signed a Russia sanctions bill and a big arms deal, and a source says he kept asking Zelensky to stop hitting refineries. They meet Tuesday. Zelensky says it “could change a lot.” What would count?
13-17.why: Two true things: the ally who arms you wants a veto. Let them argue it.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once, and the script gives them the pair: the US just signed sanctions and the biggest arms deal of Trump's term, and the same president is asking Ukraine to stop hitting refineries. Expect “why should Ukraine listen?” Because the weapons come from the same man. That is the whole tension.

5-7.a: They did, on Sunday. Some things get sorted faster when people sit at the same table.

8-12.q: Why does Trump want Ukraine to stop hitting refineries?
8-12.a: They push up diesel prices around the world, a source told Axios.

8-12.q: What are the one or two things left?
8-12.a: Axios's source didn't say. Only that the list shrank from dozens.

13-17.q: Does Trump get to pick Ukraine's targets?
13-17.a: Asking, not ordering, per Axios. Ukraine says it's ready for really serious steps.

13-17.q: What's actually left to agree on?
13-17.a: One or two key issues, says Ukraine's negotiator. He didn't name them.
